title: Quantitative analysis of H2O2 transport through purified membrane proteins
author: Wang, Schoebel, et al.
materials: All reagents and equipment needed for the reconstitution experiment are listed in Box 1. It is highly recommended to prepare all the reagents in advance.Box 1Reagents and equipment⁎Lipids (E. coli Polar Lipid Extract, Avanti Polar Lipids. inc)Reconstitution buffer (50 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris pH 8.0, with or without 1 mM EDTA)10% OG (n-Octyl-β-D-Glucoside, Anatrace)1 M NaCl0.5 M Tris pH 8.0200 U/ml HRP (type II, Sigma Aldrich)GF buffer (the buffer used to elute the protein in the last purification step, in the case of aquaporins, 200 mM NaCl and 20 mM Tris pH 8.0 was used).Bio-Beads (Bio-Beads® SM-2 Hydrophobic absorbents, Bio-Rad)S400HR Column (GE Healthcare)Ultracentrifuge (Beckman)Roller table (kept at 4°C)⁎Here we specify material successfully used for the aquaporin containing liposomes in Wang et al 2020, which does not exclude that alternatives could work equally well.Alt-text: Unlabelled box

steps.title: Produce recombinant aquaporin in Pichia
steps.instruction: Culture Pichia pastoris transformed with the aquaporin gene fused to a C‑terminal 8×His tag in a fermentor, harvest the cells and store the pellet at –20 °C for later purification.

steps.title: Lyse cells and isolate membranes
steps.instruction: Thaw the frozen cells, resuspend in 20 mM Tris, 20 mM NaCl buffer and disrupt them in a bead beater (e.g. Bio‑Spec) for 12 × 30 s with 30 s cooling between runs; collect unbroken cells by centrifugation, then ultracentrifuge the lysate at 200 000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C to pellet membranes, and resuspend the membrane pellet in 20 mM Tris‑HCl, 200 mM NaCl, 10 % glycerol buffer.

steps.title: Screen detergents for solubilization
steps.instruction: Add each detergent (CHAPS, DDM, DM, FosCholine‑12, LDAO, MNG, NG, β‑OG) drop‑wise to the membrane suspension, incubate at 4 °C for 2 h with rotation; centrifuge the mixture at 160 000 g for 30 min at 4 °C, collect supernatant and pellet for immunoblot to assess solubilization efficiency.

steps.title: Purify aquaporin via Ni‑NTA
steps.instruction: Add 10 mM imidazole to the solubilized membrane fraction, incubate with Ni‑NTA agarose for 3 h at 4 °C, then elute the aquaporin with buffer containing 20 mM HCl, 200 mM NaCl, 10 % glycerol, the chosen detergent, and 300 mM imidazole; concentrate the eluate using a VivaSpin 100 kDa centrifugal filter.

steps.title: Optional gel‑filtration polishing
steps.instruction: If higher purity is required, run the concentrated protein on a Superdex 200 Increase 10/300 GL column (GE Healthcare) and collect the monodisperse peak.

steps.title: Standardize protein concentration
steps.instruction: Determine the protein concentration by BCA assay or by measuring absorbance at 280 nm using the protein‑specific extinction coefficient, and adjust the stock to 0.3 mM for each aquaporin preparation.

steps.title: Activate Bio‑Beads
steps.instruction: Activate Bio‑Beads SM‑2 by washing with methanol, then rinse twice with Milli‑Q water, and finally equilibrate the beads in the reconstitution buffer.

steps.title: Prepare lipid stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve E. coli polar lipid extract in reconstitution buffer (50 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris, pH 8.0, with or without 1 mM EDTA) to a final concentration of 25 mg mL⁻¹; aliquot 160 µL into 2 mL tubes and store at 4 °C for up to two weeks.

steps.title: Assemble reconstitution mixtures
steps.instruction: For each 2 mL tube (liposome or proteoliposome) add the following components in the order shown, mixing gently after each addition and allowing 5 min pauses where indicated:

substeps.instruction: 160 µL lipid (25 mg mL⁻¹) – already present from the previous step
100 µL 10 % n‑Octyl‑β‑D‑Glucoside (OG); mix gently and stand 5 min until the solution becomes clear
2 µL HRP (200 U mL⁻¹, type II, Sigma‑Aldrich)
6.5 µL GF buffer (200 mM NaCl, 20 mM Tris, pH 8.0)
For proteoliposomes only: 6.5 µL aquaporin stock (0.3 mM)
300 mg activated Bio‑Beads; mix gently and wait 5 min

steps.title: Incubate reconstitution at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Place the tubes on a roller table and rotate at 4 °C for 3 h.

steps.title: Remove Bio‑Beads by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the mixtures at 13 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C using a 0.22 µm spin filter to retain the beads; collect the flow‑through.

steps.title: Pellet liposomes by ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL reconstitution buffer containing 1 mM EDTA to the flow‑through and ultracentrifuge at 140 000 × g for 45 min at 4 °C; discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash and resuspend liposomes
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL reconstitution buffer (with 1 mM EDTA), ultracentrifuge again at 140 000 × g for 45 min at 4 °C, discard the supernatant, and finally resuspend the washed liposomes in 200 µL reconstitution buffer by gentle mixing (liposomes are fragile).

steps.title: Remove external HRP with size‑exclusion column
steps.instruction: Load 100 µL of the liposome suspension onto a S400HR column (GE Healthcare) and spin at 700 × g for 30 s at 4 °C; collect the flow‑through.

steps.title: Finalize liposome preparation
steps.instruction: Mix the collected flow‑through with an additional 500 µL reconstitution buffer; the resulting proteoliposome or liposome suspension is ready for the H₂O₂ transport assay.

description: Cell-based methods for aquaporin mediated hydrogen peroxide transport include qualitative growth assays using yeast cells combined with fluorescent dyeing and fluorescent probe. These measurements rely on the expression of the channel proteins in the host cells, and, most importantly, proper localization of the recombinant protein to the cellular membrane [1], [2], [3], [4], factors that are difficult to fully control and standardize. Noteworthy, recombinant production of the 13 highly homologues plasma membrane intrinsic proteins (PIPs) isoforms from Arabidopsis thaliana in Saccharomyces cerevisiae using the expression vector pYES2 [5] resulted in major variations in protein levels (Fig. 1). In conclusion, even when using the same promoter and growth conditions, comparing transport efficiencies and specificities for the AtPIP isoforms was non-trivial using the cell-based system [6]. Furthermore, working with cell-based systems, there is a substantial risk that background reactions within the complex intracellular environment of the host cell interfere with reaction of interest and influence the final results, an aspect that is also pronounced in less complex cells like yeast. In addition, the recombinant expression as such, aiming at producing a foreign protein within the cellular environment, might have a negative impact on endogenous physiological processes which could also interfere with the analysis giving misleading results.Fig. 1Recombinant production of aquaporins in yeast for functional studies. Immunoblot showing the variation in production levels of the 13 AtPIPs expressed in yeast cells using the vector of pYES2.
